name: St. Augustine
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in St. Augustine, FL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in St. Augustine, FL: Nights of Lights, the Christmas Parade, Regatta of Lights, Ripley's Red Train and a Farmstead skating festival.
lede: St. Augustine does Christmas with Nights of Lights, a free display of more than three million white lights across the historic district, plus a Christmas parade with Santa, a lighted boat regatta on Matanzas Bay and holiday evenings at the lighthouse and the beach.
celebrates: The season centers on Nights of Lights, which Florida's Historic Coast says covers about 20 city blocks, with white lights from the sidewalks to the rooftops and over the Bridge of Lions. Light-Up Night opens it with live entertainment in front of City Hall and an official lighting ceremony at the Plaza de la Constitucion. The annual Christmas Parade follows with floats, marching groups and Santa, who poses for photos with kids at the plaza. The St. Augustine Yacht Club's Regatta of Lights fills Matanzas Bay with decorated boats, and the St. Augustine Lighthouse adds Luminary Night and Lighthouse Illuminations.
lastyear: Last year, 2025, was the 32nd season of Nights of Lights and the 67th annual Christmas Parade, counting back from the 33rd season and 68th parade that the hosts name for 2026. Visit St. Augustine says the Regatta of Lights always falls on the second Saturday of December, so it held the same place on the calendar in 2025. The lights themselves now number more than three million, according to the city and the tourism bureau.
facts: Florida's Historic Coast calls Nights of Lights one of the top light displays in the world, and the 2026 season is its 33rd. Visit St. Augustine calls the Christmas Parade a tradition of more than 60 years and names this year's its 68th annual. Henry Flagler opened the Ponce de Leon Hotel on January 10, 1888, in a city he found charming but short on hotels and transportation, and his railroad helped bring winter visitors to town.
trains: St. Augustine's Christmas has a railroad story. Henry Flagler took over the Jacksonville, St. Augustine and Halifax River Railway in the winter of 1885 and 1886, and the Florida East Coast Railway grew from that line. Its freight trains still run over nearly the same route he developed, and its offices moved to Jacksonville after the St. Augustine general office building was sold in 2006. For a ride today, Ripley's Red Train Tours runs a 30 minute Nights of Lights tour.
train_links: The 1919 rail terminal in Jacksonville, now the Prime F. Osborn III Convention Center.
Volunteers sharing Florida East Coast Railway history, with free public events.
traditions: More than three million white lights across about 20 blocks of the historic district, from late November into January.
A lighting ceremony at the Plaza de la Constitucion that opens the season.
Floats, marching groups and Santa, ending with Santa photos for kids at the Plaza de la Constitucion.

kidfact: Look for two photo spots the host suggests: the big Christmas tree in the middle of the Plaza de la Constitucion, and the Bridge of Lions, where the lights shine again in the water.
faq: What is Nights of Lights in St. Augustine?

Nights of Lights is the city's holiday display of more than three million white lights across about 20 blocks of the historic district. The lights go from the sidewalks to the rooftops, over the Bridge of Lions and along hotels and inns. It starts in late November and runs into January, and Florida's Historic Coast calls it one of the top displays in the world.

Yes. Walking the lit streets is free and no tickets are needed. Tours are separate and booked with each company, including Old Town Trolley, Ripley's Red Train Tours, character carriage rides and boat tours. Families can also join free walking tours and see the lights from the Lightner Museum's free 360 video experience, which the hosts list.
Where do families park for Nights of Lights?

Downtown parking fills up fast. The City of St. Augustine runs a free Park and Ride shuttle on select days from lots at 200 San Sebastian View, 198 West King Street and 301 San Marco Avenue, with drop off at the Visitor Information Center at 10 South Castillo Drive. Check the city's shuttle page for the days and hours.
Can kids meet Santa in St. Augustine?

Yes, in several places. Santa joins the annual Christmas Parade and poses for photos with kids at the Plaza de la Constitucion afterward. The lighthouse's Luminary Night lists a visit with Santa, the Ancient City Farmstead has Santa's Workshop photos, and Magical Ride with Santa is a ticketed holiday ride.
Are there train rides at Christmas in St. Augustine?

Ripley's Red Train Tours runs a 30 minute Nights of Lights ride that boards at Ripley's Believe It or Not on San Marco Avenue, with holiday music and magic glasses for riders. It is a road train, sold by the seat, so book ahead. For real railroad history, see the Florida East Coast Railway guide linked here.
Where does the St. Augustine Christmas Parade go?

The annual Christmas Parade starts at the Mission Nombre de Dios at 27 Ocean Avenue, goes south through downtown and ends behind the Visitor Information Center at 10 West Castillo Drive. Visit St. Augustine recommends watching from the west side of San Marco Avenue, along Cathedral Place or on Cordova Street.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in St. Augustine for 2026, and here is what he found: 13 family events, 7 of them free. The magic runs from November 20 (Lighthouse Illuminations: Tides, Tidings and Trees) through January 18 (Nights of Lights), with the Christmas Parade (December 5), the Holiday Regatta of Lights (December 12) and the Christmas Experience at Ancient City Farmstead (December 12) along the way. We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there.

What Rally found in St. Augustine

  • 13 Christmas events for kids in St. Augustine
  • 7 free events, including Nights of Lights, the Christmas Parade and the Holiday Regatta of Lights
  • Meet Santa: Magical Ride with Santa, Christmas with Cops and Claus and Luminary Night at the lighthouse
  • Parades and lights: Christmas Parade, Holiday Regatta of Lights, Hastings Hometown Christmas Parade and Nights of Lights
  • Trains: Nights of Lights Tour on Ripley's Red Train (a road train, not a railroad)
  • Season: November 20, 2026 to January 18, 2027
